Vertical: YesHorizontal: UnknownOblique: Unknown
Evidence and details

Description: Chimpanzees live in semi-wild conditions in CWOT. Handclasping occurs during grooming, which whimps reach overhead and clasp hands while grooming with the other hand. This has been observed in 16 independent populations at time of study in 2010 which observed variation in ecologically homogeneous but socially separate groups in CWOT. Wrist-to-wrist style of GHC more frequent in group 1 compared with group 2.

Vertical: "The assessment of the GHC transmission showed that 20 juveniles (11 females) out of the 23 juveniles in the handclasp groups (11 females) started engaging in the GHC behaviour and that in 83 per cent of the possible cases the mother was the first partner of these new handclaspers" (van Leeuwen et al. 2012)

Horizontal: suspected unknown

Oblique: suspected unknown

Domains: social

Anthropogenic effects: semi-wild populations consisting of wild-born and sanctuary-raised individuals

Sources: [1]

Vertical: YesHorizontal: UnknownOblique: Unknown
Evidence and details

Description: Chimpanzees live in semi-wild conditions in CWOT. Handclasping occurs during grooming, which whimps reach overhead and clasp hands while grooming with the other hand. This has been observed in 16 independent populations at time of study in 2010 which observed variation in ecologically homogeneous but socially separate groups in CWOT. Palm-to-palm style of GHC more frequent in group 1 compared with group 2.

Vertical: "The assessment of the GHC transmission showed that 20 juveniles (11 females) out of the 23 juveniles in the handclasp groups (11 females) started engaging in the GHC behaviour and that in 83 per cent of the possible cases the mother was the first partner of these new handclaspers" (van Leeuwen et al. 2012)

Horizontal: suspected unknown

Oblique: suspected unknown

Domains: social

Anthropogenic effects: semi-wild populations consisting of wild-born and CWOT-raised individuals
